key_insight: Special martensitic deformations enable elastic Landau states that assemble into closed, arbitrarily shaped, stress-free martensitic islands within austenite.
engineering_relevance: The theory offers geometric guidance for designing self-accommodating microstructures in shape-memory alloys, including through hierarchical twinning.
method: Derive two-parameter deformation families that permit closed, stress-free austenite–martensite interfaces.
Interpret simple shear and pure shear as cubic-to-monoclinic-II and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations.
Construct elastic Landau states using extreme compatibility and consider hierarchical twins with simple-shear average deformation.
evidence_signal: Predicted deformation gradients agree with those reconstructed from experimentally observed microstructures, although the abstract reports no quantitative agreement metrics.
watch_item: Geometric compatibility alone does not establish whether the proposed nuclei can form under realistic energetic and kinetic constraints.
paper_title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
